new_item_identified_this_pass.status: Unresolved -- not a cross-file/cross-source discrepancy and not something a further reverification round would fix, so not sent back per the one-round rule. Flagged here for visibility only.
new_item_identified_this_pass.finding: I independently recomputed the implied denominator from the raw PNG figures: CVC Credit Partners' EUR91,460,000 / 4.76% implies an instrument size of ~EUR1.921bn; PGIM's EUR54,317,000 / 2.83% implies ~EUR1.919bn -- both consistently pointing to an implied base of roughly EUR1.92bn, not the stated EUR1,020m facility size (9fin cap table). By contrast, the USD 500m 2031 SSN holder table reconciles exactly (top-10 amounts sum to USD136.8m against a reported cumulative 27.36%, and USD136.8m / USD500m = 27.36%). This looks like a genuine anomaly in how 9fin's 'Holders and Transactions' UI computed the % column for this specific (EUR TLB) instrument in the screenshot -- possibly a blended/cross-currency TLB denominator -- rather than any inconsistency between capital.json, financials.json or news.json. researcher-capital has already transcribed the figures faithfully from the primary source and flagged the anomaly transparently in both holdings.data_quality_flag and data_gaps, consistent with the 'mark it, don't infer' rule. No further action recommended other than the diligence path already noted (9fin support query on the % of instrument methodology for this deal).
